verdict.rationale: Alacritty's own docs cover font tuning: family and style per face, size in points, and x/y offsets for letter and line spacing. It also uses a custom built-in font for box-drawing and legacy computing symbols. However, the vendor makes no claim of ligature support, and community users describe the long-standing 'ligature issue' as unsupported. Missing for 10: ligature support, documented user-configurable fallback fonts, and independent corroboration of tuning depth beyond one comment that font rendering is great.

support.subject: As a developer, I can use programming fonts with ligatures, fallback fonts, and fine-grained font tuning

citations.quote: normal = { family = "<string>", style = "<string>" } ... size = <float> Font size in points.
Offset is the extra space around each character. y can be thought of as modifying the line spacing, and x as modifying the letter spacing.
Alacritty will use a custom built-in font for box drawing characters (Unicode points U+2500 - U+259F), legacy computing symbols
